name: Efficient App

sources.title: Submit Your App on App Stacks — two-step flow ending in a one-time evaluation fee; 'we can't guarantee that your product will get selected'; response in 5–7 business days
About — heavy curation: hands-on testing, interviews founders, only lists apps they'd 'proudly recommend'

requirements: Submission is really a paid evaluation: a one-time fee buys deep evaluation, NOT a guaranteed listing
App must pass editorial bar — they test firsthand and only list tools that fit the quality of existing picks
Better odds if existing listed apps already integrate/serve your customers
B2B/team software focus (software stacks for teams)
preparation: Product must be genuinely good — this site stakes its brand on recommendations
Step 1 asks for product basics + contact email ('used to contact you if your product gets selected')
Payment method for the one-time evaluation fee (amount not shown in indexed snippet — confirm on page)
Evidence of quality: customer logos, integrations with tools already on the site
workflow: Step 2: pay the one-time evaluation fee
Wait 5–7 business days for the team's decision
If selected, the app appears in relevant stack/category pages; other teams can add it to their tool stacks
watchFor: Payment does NOT buy a listing — it buys evaluation. Rejected fees may not be refunded (policy unstated)
Highly curated — most submissions likely rejected; treat as a long-shot credibility play, not a bulk directory
Efficient.app homepage rate-limited automated fetches (429) during research
Listing benefit is endorsement + stack inclusion, more credibility than raw traffic
countsAsLive: The app appears on efficient.app / stacks.efficient.app app pages or within category stacks after editorial selection
unknowns: Exact evaluation fee amount (page indexed but price not captured)
Whether listed apps get followed outbound links
